title: DECREE ON DISCIPLINARY ACTION AGAINST POLICE OFFICIALS
full_text:
DECREE ON DISCIPLINARY ACTION AGAINST POLICE OFFICIALS

 

 
 Presidential Decree No. 32534, Mar. 15, 2022 

 

 

 

 Presidential Decree No. 32534, Mar. 15, 2022

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 1 (Purpose)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters necessary for disciplinary action against police officials under 
Articles 32 and 33 of the Police Officials Act
 and the imposition of additional disciplinary charges under 
Article 78-2 of the State Public Officials Act
. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2020>
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 2 (Definitions)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The terms used in this Decree are defined as follows:
1.
 The term "severe disciplinary action" means removal, dismissal, demotion, and suspension from office;
2.
 The term "light disciplinary action" means salary reduction and reprimand.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 3 (Types and establishment of disciplinary committees)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Disciplinary committees for police officials shall be classified into the Central Disciplinary Committee for Police Officials (hereinafter referred to as the "Central Disciplinary Committee") and the General Disciplinary Committee for Police Officials (hereinafter referred to as the "General Disciplinary Committee").
(2)
 The Central Disciplinary Committee shall be established in the Korean National Police Agency and the Korea Coast Guard, and the General Disciplinary Committee shall be established in the Korean National Police Agency, the Korea Coast Guard, a City/
Do
 police agency, a regional coast guard, the Korean National Police University, the Police Human Resources Development Institute, the Central Police Academy, the Korean Police Investigation Academy, the Korea Coast Guard Academy, the National Police Hospital, a police station, a mobile police unit, an auxiliary police company, a coast guard station, the Korea Coast Guard Maintenance Center, a patrol ship, or an agency headed by a Senior Inspector or higher-ranking police official designated by the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency or the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard. <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017; Mar. 30, 2018; Dec. 31, 2020>
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 4 (Jurisdiction of disciplinary committees)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The Central Disciplinary Committee shall deliberate and resolve on disciplinary actions against Senior Superintendents and Superintendents or the imposition of additional disciplinary charges under 
Article 78-2 of the State Public Officials Act
 (hereinafter referred to as "disciplinary action, etc.")
(2)
 The General Disciplinary Committee shall deliberate and resolve on cases involving disciplinary action, etc. against Senior Inspectors or lower-ranking police officials within the police agency where the relevant disciplinary committee is established; provided, the General Disciplinary Committee established in the following agencies shall deliberate and resolve on cases involving disciplinary action, etc. against police officials classified as follows: <Amended on Nov. 19, 2014; Nov. 20, 2015; Jul. 26, 2017>
1.
 Police stations headed by Superintendents or higher-ranking police officials, police agencies, such as mobile police units and coast guard stations, or maintenance centers headed by Senior Superintendents or higher-ranking police officials: Inspectors or lower-ranking police officials;
2.
 Police agencies, such as auxiliary police companies and patrol vessels, headed by Senior Inspectors or higher-ranking police officials designated by the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency or the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard: Assistant Inspectors or lower-ranking police officials affiliated with those agencies.
(3)
 Notwithstanding paragraph (2), the General Disciplinary Committee established in the Korean National Police Agency and the Korea Coast Guard shall deliberate and resolve on cases involving disciplinary action, etc. against police officials as requested by the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency or the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard to be resolved. <Amended on Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017>
(4)
 Cases involving disciplinary action, etc. against a police official who falls outside the jurisdiction of the relevant General Disciplinary Committee pursuant to the proviso of paragraph (2) or the proviso of 
Article 6
 (2) shall be deliberated and resolved on by the General Disciplinary Committee established in the immediately-superior police agency.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 5 (Jurisdiction over related cases)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Notwithstanding 
Article 4
, cases involving disciplinary action, etc. related to higher-ranking and lower-ranking police officials shall be deliberated and resolved on by the disciplinary committee having jurisdiction over higher-ranking police officials, and cases involving police officials from higher-level and lower-level police agencies shall be deliberated and resolved on by the disciplinary committee established within the higher-level police agencies; provided, if a case only involves supervisory negligence by a higher-ranking police official, the competent disciplinary committee under 
Article 4
 may deliberate and resolve on such case.
(2)
 If a case involving disciplinary action, etc. is related to at least 2 police officials with different affiliations, where the competent disciplinary committees differ, the disciplinary committee established at the immediately superior police agency having jurisdiction over all those officials shall deliberate and resolve on the case.
(3)
 Notwithstanding 
Article 4
 (2), cases involving disciplinary action, etc. related to violations under 
Article 37 (1) or (2) of the Police Officials Act
 may be deliberated and resolved on by the General Disciplinary Committee established in the Korean National Police Agency, the Korea Coast Guard, a City/
Do
 police agency, or a regional coast guard. <Amended on Nov. 19, 2014; Jul. 26, 2017; Dec. 31, 2020>
(4)
 Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) and (2), if the competent disciplinary committee under paragraphs (1) and (2) deems it appropriate to separately deliberate and resolve on a case involving disciplinary action, etc. against a relevant person, the case may be transferred to the competent disciplinary committee under 
Article 4
 by resolution of the relevant disciplinary committee.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 6 (Composition of disciplinary committee)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Each disciplinary committee shall consist of at least 11 but not more than 51 members who are public officials and civilians, including 1 chairperson. <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020>
(2)
 The head of a police agency in which a disciplinary committee is established may appoint a public official member of the disciplinary committee from among Inspectors or police officials of a higher rank than those subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. or public officials of Grade VI or higher rank; provided, in cases of a general disciplinary committee, if it is difficult to organize such committee because the number of Inspectors or police officials of a higher rank than those subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. or if public officials of Grade VI or higher rank falls short of the number of members excluding civilian members referred to in paragraph (3), appointment may be made from among police officials of Assistant Inspectors or a lower rank or public officials of Grade VII or lower, and in such cases, notwithstanding 
Article 4
 (2), cases involving salary reduction or reprimand for not more than 3 months shall be deliberated on and resolved.
(3)
 The head of the police agency where a disciplinary committee is established shall appoint at least 1/2 of the members referred to in paragraph (1) as civilian members from among those falling under the following subparagraphs; in such cases, no more than 6/10 of the civilian members shall belong to 1 gender: <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020; Mar. 15, 2022>
1.
 The Central Disciplinary Committee;
(a)
 A person who has served as a judge, public prosecutor, or attorney-at-law for at least 10 years;
(b)
 A person who currently serves as a full-time professor or higher, specializing in police-related studies at a school under 
Article 2 of the Higher Education Act
 or an educational institution corresponding thereto (hereinafter referred to as "university or college");
(c)
 A person who has served as a Senior Superintendent or public official of Grade IV or higher before retirement [(referring to a person for whom 3 years have elapsed since retirement, if he or she served in the police agency for 5 years before retirement (including cases where he or she has served at a central administrative agency or at another affiliated agency of the relevant police agency)];
(d)
 A person who held an executive officer or equivalent position in charge of personnel affairs and audits in the private sector;
2.
 The General Disciplinary Committee:
(a)
 A person who has served as a judge, public prosecutor, or attorney-at-law for at least 5 years;
(b)
 A person who currently serves as an associate professor or higher at a university or college, specializing in police-related studies;
(c)
 A person who has served as a public official for at least 20 years before retirement [(referring to a person for whom 3 years have elapsed since retirement, if he or she has served in the police agency for 5 years before retirement (including cases where he or she has served at a central administrative agency or at another affiliated agency of the relevant police agency)];
(d)
 A person who held an executive officer or equivalent position in charge of personnel affairs and audits in the private sector;
(4)
 The chairperson of a disciplinary committee shall be a public official of the highest rank or a corresponding class or the person first promoted to such rank or class, from among its members. <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020>
[This Article Wholly Amended on Oct. 22, 2013]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 6-2 (Term of office of members)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
The term of office of civilian members commissioned pursuant to 
Article 6
 (3) shall be 2 years, and they may be reappointed only once.
[This Article Newly Inserted on Oct. 22, 2013]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 7 (Meetings of disciplinary committees)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 A disciplinary committee meeting shall consist of at least 4 but not more than 6 members designated by the chairperson and the head of the police agency where the committee is established, taking into account gender equality, and civilian members shall constitute at least 1/2 of all members, including the chairperson. <Newly Inserted on Jun. 16, 2020>
(2)
 If a disciplinary committee meeting is convened to deal with any of the following disciplinary cases, at least 1/3 of the committee members, excluding the chairperson, shall be of the same gender as the victim: <Newly Inserted on Mar. 15, 2022>
1.
 Sexual crimes under the 
Act on Special Cases concerning the Punishment of Sexual Crimes
;
2.
 Sexual harassment under the 
Framework Act on Gender Equality
.
(3)
 The chairperson of the disciplinary committee shall represent the committee and exercise general supervision over its affairs. <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020; Mar. 15, 2022>
(4)
 Meetings of the disciplinary committee shall be convened by the chairperson. <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020; Mar. 15, 2022>
(5)
 The chairperson shall have the right to vote. <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020; Mar. 15, 2022>
(6)
 If the chairperson is unable to perform his or her duties due to any unavoidable reason or if deemed necessary by him or her, the public official of the highest or equivalent rank among those present, or the first person promoted to such rank shall serve as the acting chairperson. <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020; Mar. 15, 2022>
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]
[Moved from Article 8; previous Article 7 moved to Article 8 <Jun. 16, 2020>]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 8 (Executive secretary of disciplinary committee)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 A disciplinary committee shall have several executive secretaries.
(2)
 The executive secretaries shall be appointed by the head of the police agency where the relevant disciplinary committee is established, from among public officials under his or her jurisdiction (excluding those in charge of investigating cases involving disciplinary action, etc.). <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020>
(3)
 The executive secretary shall prepare and preserve the records of cases involving disciplinary action, etc. and other documents, as directed by the chairperson.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]
[Moved from Article 7; previous Article 8 moved to Article 7 <Jun. 16, 2020>]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 9 (Request for resolution on disciplinary action)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 If a police official falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the head of a police agency shall, without delay, establish a competent disciplinary committee and request the committee to pass a resolution on disciplinary action, etc.; in such cases, the head of the agency shall submit to the competent committee a written request for a resolution on disciplinary action against police officials in attached Form 1 or a written confirmation in attached Form 1-2 (hereafter in this Article referred to as "written resolution on disciplinary action, etc."):
1.
 When it is deemed that there is a ground for disciplinary action falling under any of 
Article 78 (1) 1 through 3 of the State Public Officials Act
 (hereinafter referred to as "grounds for disciplinary action");
2.
 When he or she receives an application for a request for a resolution on other disciplinary action, etc. under paragraph (2).
(2)
 The head of the police agency shall, if a case involving a disciplinary action, etc. against a police official under his or her jurisdiction falls under the jurisdiction of a disciplinary committee established at a superior police agency, apply for a request for a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. to the head of the superior agency, along with a written resolution on disciplinary action, etc.
(3)
 A request, or application for a request, for a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be made after conducting sufficient investigation into the grounds for disciplinary action.
(4)
 When making, or applying for, a request for a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2), the head of a police agency shall classify violations as either a severe or light disciplinary action; provided, this shall not apply where the Chairperson of the Board of Audit and Inspection makes a request for a disciplinary action by specifying the types of disciplinary action under 
Article 79 of the State Public Officials Act
 pursuant to 
Article 32 (1) and (10) of the Board of Audit and Inspection Act
.
(5)
 If the head of a police agency requests a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. pursuant to paragraph (1), he or she shall send a copy of the written request for a resolution on disciplinary action against a police official or on the imposition of an additional disciplinary charge under paragraph (1) to the person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc.; provided, this shall not apply if the person refuses to accept such request.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Oct. 22, 2013]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 10 (Notification of cases involving disciplinary action)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 If the head of a police agency deems that a police official not affiliated with his or her police agency has committed an act which constitutes the grounds for disciplinary action, he or she shall notify the head of the relevant police agency of such decision clearly providing sufficient grounds to support the decision.
(2)
 The head of the police agency who is notified of the grounds for disciplinary action pursuant to paragraph (1) shall either request the competent disciplinary committee to pass a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. or apply for the request to the head of a superior agency within 30 days of receiving such notification pursuant to 
Article 9
, unless there is good reason. <Amended on Oct. 22, 2013>
(3)
 Upon receiving notification of the grounds for disciplinary action pursuant to paragraph (1), the head of the police agency shall inform the head of the notifying police agency of the results of handling the relevant case.
(4)
 Deleted. <Oct. 22, 2013>
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 11 (Deadline for resolution on disciplinary action)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Upon receiving a request for a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. a disciplinary committee shall pass a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. within 30 days of receiving such request; provided, if there is any unavoidable reason, the deadline may be extended by up to 30 days with the approval of the head of the police agency that requested the resolution on the relevant disciplinary action, etc. <Amended on Mar. 15, 2022>
(2)
 If the procedures for disciplinary action, etc. in a case where a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. was requested are suspended pursuant to 
Article 83 of the State Public Officials Act
, the suspension period shall not count toward the deadline for resolution on disciplinary action, etc. under paragraph (1).
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 12 (Attendance of persons subject to deliberation on disciplinary action)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 When a disciplinary committee requests the attendance of a person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc., a notice of attendance in attached Form 2 shall be provided, and it shall be delivered to the person at least 5 days before the scheduled committee meeting. <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020>
(2)
 If the person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. does not wish to appear before the disciplinary committee and make a statement, the disciplinary committee may require him or her to submit a written waiver of the right to make a statement, attach it to the records, and may proceed with a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. based on a written review.
(3)
 If the person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. fails to appear before the disciplinary committee without good cause despite the notice of attendance, the disciplinary committee may clearly record such fact and pass a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. through written review; provided, if the whereabouts of the person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. are unknown, the notice of attendance shall be published in the Official Gazette, and the notice shall be deemed served after 10 days from the date of publication, and if the disciplinary committee passes a resolution on disciplinary action, etc., the reasons for publishing the notice in the Official Gazette and the fact of publication shall be clearly recorded. <Amended on Oct. 22, 2013>
(4)
 Notwithstanding paragraph (3), if it is deemed impracticable to personally deliver a written notice of attendance to the person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. or his or her family because he or she has fled for the purpose of evading the fact-finding investigation in a case involving disciplinary action, etc. or criminal case or because he or she has refused to receive such notice, the disciplinary committee shall send the notice to the head of an agency the person is affiliated with so as to ensure its delivery, and if the delivery is impracticable or the person refuses to accept such notice, the head shall ensure that such fact is reported with supporting documents attached and may pass a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. based on a written review.
(5)
 If the person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. is deemed unable to appear within a reasonable period from the date of receipt of a written request for a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. due to being abroad for stay or travel, or any other unavoidable reason, the disciplinary committee may pass a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. by requiring him or her to make a written statement within an appropriate period, notwithstanding 
Article 11
. In such cases, if he or she fails to make the written statement within such period, the committee may proceed with a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. without the written statement.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 13 (Right of interrogation and statement)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The disciplinary committee may interrogate a person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. who has appeared pursuant to 
Article 12
 (1) about the facts that constitute the grounds for disciplinary action, etc., and if deemed necessary for review, may summon and interrogate other relevant persons.
(2)
 The disciplinary committee shall provide the person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. with ample opportunity to make a statement, and the person may state facts in his or her favor either through the written opinion in attached Form 2-2 or in his or her own words or submit evidence. <Amended on Aug. 6, 2019>
(3)
 The person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. may apply for the interrogation of a witness. In such cases, the disciplinary committee shall decide whether to adopt such application by resolution.
(4)
 A person who has requested a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. or a person who has applied for such request may attend the disciplinary committee meeting to state his or her opinion or submit the same in writing; provided, in the case of cases involving severe disciplinary actions or those involving requests for additional disciplinary charges related to severe disciplinary actions, he or she shall attend the disciplinary committee meeting and state his or her opinion unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. <Amended on Mar. 15, 2022>
(5)
 The disciplinary committee may, if deemed necessary, conduct a fact-finding investigation or request the verification or approval from a person with special knowledge and experience.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 14 (Resolution by disciplinary committee)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 A resolution of a disciplinary committee shall be passed with the attendance of a majority of the members including the chairperson and the concurring vote of a majority of those present, but if opinions are divided and the consent of a majority of those present is not obtained, the opinions of the members with the most unfavorable views toward the person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. shall be added in turn to those who presented the next most unfavorable opinion until a majority is formed, and the resulting opinion shall be deemed a consensus opinion. <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020>
(2)
 The resolution under paragraph (1) shall be documented in a written resolution on disciplinary action or on additional disciplinary charges in attached Form 3 (hereinafter referred to as "written resolution"); in such cases, the following matters shall be specified in the column entitled reasons for the written resolution: <Amended on Oct. 22, 2013; Aug. 6, 2019; Mar. 15, 2022>
1.
 The fact leading to the disciplinary action, etc.;
2.
 Judgment on evidence;
4.
 Relevant statutes or regulations;
4.
 Applicability of any grounds for exemption from disciplinary action, etc.;
5.
 Reasons for adjustment (reduction or exemption) of additional disciplinary charges.
(3)
 Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the disciplinary committee may pass a resolution in writing on the following matters: <Newly Inserted on Mar. 15, 2022>
1.
 Transfer of jurisdiction over cases involving disciplinary action, etc. under 
Article 5
 (4);
2.
 Extension of the deadline for a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. under 
Article 11
 (1).
(4)
 Matters relating to the procedures, methods, etc. for a written resolution under paragraph (3) shall be determined by the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency. <Newly Inserted on Mar. 15, 2022>
(5)
 The details of the disciplinary committee's resolutions shall not be disclosed. <Amended on Mar. 15, 2022>
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 14-2 (Utilization of remote video conferencing methods)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 The disciplinary committee may conduct deliberations and resolutions via remote video conferencing, where those attending meetings under this Decree, such as the committee members, the person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc., the person requesting, or applying for a request, for a resolution, witnesses, and other relevant persons (hereafter in this paragraph referred to as "attendees"), are located in different places equipped with devices capable of simultaneous transmission and reception of video and audio. In such cases, the committee members and the attendees shall be deemed present at the same meeting venue.
(2)
 If the disciplinary committee deliberates and resolves via remote video conferencing in accordance with paragraph (1), it shall take necessary security measures to prevent the leakage of personal information of the members and attendees, the details and results of the meeting, and other relevant information.
(3)
 Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), matters necessary for the operation of remote video conferencing shall be determined by the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency.
[This Article Newly Inserted on Mar. 15, 2022]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 15 (Exclusion, challenge, or recusal)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 If the chairperson or a member of a disciplinary committee falls under any of the following subparagraphs, he or she shall not participate in the deliberation and resolution on a relevant case involving disciplinary action, etc.: <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020>
1.
 Where he or she is a relative or direct superior of the person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. (including a person who was a direct superior during the period in which the grounds for disciplinary action arose);
2.
 Where he or she is related to the grounds for disciplinary action;
3.
 Where he or she participated in the investigation of, or the deliberation or resolution on, the relevant case involving disciplinary action, etc., when the case was reconsidered for reasons under 
Article 78-3 (1) 3 of the State Public Officials Act
.
(2)
 If the chairperson or a member of the disciplinary committee falls under any of the following, a person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. may notify the committee in writing of such fact and file a motion for challenge to the chairperson or the committee member: <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020>
1.
 Where he or she falls under any subparagraph of paragraph (1);
2.
 Where there are reasonable grounds to suspect that his or her involvement may result in an unfair resolution.
(3)
 Upon receiving the motion for challenge filed under paragraph (2), the disciplinary committee shall determine whether to challenge the relevant chairperson or member by resolution before deliberating on the relevant case involving disciplinary action, etc. In such cases, the chairperson or the member challenged shall not participate in the resolution. <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020>
(4)
 If the chairperson or a member of the disciplinary committee falls under any subparagraph of paragraph (1), he or she shall voluntarily recuse himself or herself from deliberation and resolution on the relevant case, and if he or she falls under paragraph (2) 2, he or she may recuse himself or herself. <Amended on Jun. 16, 2020>
(5)
 When the disciplinary committee cannot be properly constituted due to exclusions, challenges, or recusals under paragraphs (1) through (4), it shall request the head of the relevant police agency to appoint additional members.
(6)
 In cases falling under paragraph (5), the head of the relevant police agency shall, without delay, appoint additional members; provided, if it is impracticable to appoint additional members, the request for a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. shall be withdrawn, and an application for the request shall be filed with the head of a superior police agency.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 16 (Severity of disciplinary action)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
When resolving on a case involving disciplinary action, etc., the disciplinary committee shall take into account the rank and position of the person subject to deliberation on disciplinary action, etc. the impact of his or her misconduct both within and outside the public office, his or her usual behavior and achievements, the degree of his or her repentance, and other relevant circumstances, and the opinions of the person who has requested the resolution on disciplinary action, etc. <Amended on Mar. 15, 2022>
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 17 (Notification of resolution on disciplinary action)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
Upon passing a resolution on disciplinary action, etc., it shall, without delay, notify the person who has requested the resolution by delivering an authentic copy of the written resolution.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 18 (Execution of light disciplinary action)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Upon receiving notification of a resolution on light disciplinary action, etc. the person who has requested the resolution shall execute the disciplinary action, etc. within 15 days of receiving the notification.
(2)
 When executing a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. under paragraph (1), the person who has requested the resolution shall send a copy of the written resolution to the person subject to the disciplinary action, etc., along with a written explanation of the grounds for the disciplinary action, etc. in attached Form 4.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 19 (Recommendation for, and execution of, disposition to impose severe disciplinary action)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 Upon receiving notification of a resolution on severe disciplinary action, etc. a person who requested the resolution on disciplinary action, etc. shall, without delay, recommend a disposition to impose the relevant disciplinary action, etc. by sending an authentic copy of the written resolution to the person authorized to appoint the person subject to the disposition of disciplinary action, etc.; provided, the recommendation for demotion or suspension from office of Superintendent Generals or higher, the recommendation for removal or dismissal from office of Superintendents or higher, and the execution of the demotion or suspension from office of Senior Superintendents or Superintendents shall be conducted by the Commissioner General of the National Police Agency or the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard. <Amended on Nov. 19, 2014, on Jul. 26, 2017>
(2)
 Upon receiving a recommendation for severe disciplinary action under paragraph (1), the appointing authority shall provide, within 15 days, the person subject to the disciplinary action, etc., with a copy of the written resolution, accompanied by the written explanation of the grounds for the disciplinary action, etc. using attached Form 4.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 20 (Reporting and notification)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
When the head of a police agency that has requested a resolution on disciplinary action, etc. executes a light disciplinary action, etc., he or she shall, without delay, report the result thereof to the appointing authority, attaching a copy of the written resolution, and shall notify the head of the police agency affiliated with the person subjected to the disciplinary action, etc. of the execution of such action.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 21 (Prohibition of disclosure of confidential information)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
No person who attends a disciplinary committee meeting shall disclose any confidential information acquired in the course of performing duties.
[This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 26, 2012]

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
법령보기 화면

 

 

 
 Article 22 (Matters to be observed by participants in meetings)

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 
(1)
 A person who attends a disciplinary committee meeting shall not bring the following items:
1.
 Devices capable of recording, videotaping, or photographing, such as recorders, cameras, and mobile phones;
2.
 Dangerous objects, such as deadly weapons;
3.
 Other items unrelated to the deliberation on cases involving disciplinary action, etc.
(2)
 A person who attends a disciplinary committee meeting shall not engage in the following acts:
1.
 Recording, videotaping, photographing, or relay broadcasting;
2.
